The strong demand, which translated to a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.71 times, indicates sustained investor appetite for high-yielding government securities, particularly longer-dated instruments.
Data from the auction results showed that the apex bank allotted N3.854 trillion across the three tenors, representing 2.57 times the amount offered, in what signals its continued effort to mop up excess liquidity from the financial system.
A breakdown of the results showed that the 329-day instrument attracted the highest subscription of N2.82 trillion, accounting for about 69.3 per cent of the total bids received.
The CBN offered N500 billion on the instrument but recorded subscriptions of N2.82 trillion, out of which N2.79 trillion was allotted at a stop rate of 15.99 per cent.
The 252-day instrument also recorded subscriptions above its offer, attracting N791.5 billion against N500 billion offered. The apex bank sold N783.5 billion at a stop rate of 16.68 per cent.
However, demand for the 154-day instrument fell below the amount offered, as subscriptions stood at N457.89 billion against N500 billion on offer.
The CBN allotted N280.76 billion on the instrument at a stop rate of 17.44 per cent.
The auction results showed a declining stop-rate structure across the three maturities, with the 154-day instrument recording the highest rate of 17.44 per cent, followed by 16.68 per cent on the 252-day bill and 15.99 per cent on the 329-day instrument.
Despite the differences in stop rates, the true yields remained relatively close across the instruments, settling at 18.83 per cent, 18.85 per cent and 18.68 per cent for the 154-day, 252-day and 329-day bills, respectively.
The strong preference for the 329-day instrument suggests that investors are willing to commit funds for longer periods to secure prevailing returns, amid expectations of possible changes in monetary conditions.
The scale of the allotment, particularly on the longest tenor, also highlights the CBN’s willingness to absorb liquidity beyond its initial auction target.
With total sales exceeding the offer by N2.35 trillion, the auction represents another significant liquidity management operation by the apex bank.
The development comes as investors continue to position their portfolios around attractive fixed-income returns, with demand concentrated on longer-dated instruments offering relatively competitive yields.
